observations.claim: SBIC East is Tokyo Small and Medium Business Investment & Consultation Co., Ltd., founded 1963-11-15; its official profile describes an East-Japan service area and shareholder categories including local governments, chambers of commerce, financial institutions and business companies.
limitations: No complete beneficial-ownership or ultimate-control analysis.

observations.claim: SBIC Central is Nagoya Small and Medium Business Investment & Consultation Co., Ltd., founded 1963-11-18, with an official service area of Aichi, Gifu, Mie, Toyama and Ishikawa.
limitations: No complete beneficial-ownership or ultimate-control analysis.

observations.claim: SBIC West is Osaka Small and Medium Business Investment & Consultation Co., Ltd., founded 1963-11-20, with an official 24-prefecture service area; its profile describes the three regional SBIC companies as sister companies.
limitations: No complete beneficial-ownership or ultimate-control analysis.

observations.claim: The three regional SBICs are distinct legal companies with separate regional mandates. Their cited official profiles do not identify them as SBI Holdings subsidiaries or affiliates; no SBI Holdings affiliation is established by these sources.
limitations: This is not a complete Japanese corporate-registry or beneficial-ownership search; absence from cited profiles is not proof that no indirect relationship could exist.

observations.claim: SBI Holdings identifies SBI Ripple Asia as a joint venture between SBI Group and Ripple and reports 60% aggregate voting rights for SBI Group; the note aggregates SBI and subsidiaries treated as subsidiaries under IFRS, so it does not prove a direct 60% holding by SBI Holdings parent alone.
limitations: No complete shareholder register or direct-versus-indirect ownership schedule captured.

observations.claim: Ripple's official SBI Ripple Asia page explicitly says SBI Ripple Asia does not handle cryptoasset XRP; the described role is marketing RippleNet software services to financial institutions and remittance companies.
limitations: Ripple is an interested JV party; this is an issuer statement, not independent operational audit evidence.

observations.claim: Ripple separately describes ODL use with XRP in Japan involving SBI Remit, Coins.ph and SBI VC Trade; these are distinct entities and service roles from SBI Ripple Asia.
limitations: No corridor-level XRP settlement volume, wallet balance, net flow or collateral amount disclosed.

observations.claim: SBI Ripple Asia announced a proof of concept for tokenized deposits/deposit-based digital money using MoneyTap infrastructure and a token-issuance platform with XRPL contemplated as blockchain; this is not evidence of production deployment or live bank deposit issuance.
limitations: No production launch, customer volume, deposits outstanding or XRP usage established.

observations.claim: Ripple announced RLUSD availability in Japan through SBI VC Trade after JFSA approval under the Payment Services Act; Ripple reported USD 1.7B RLUSD market capitalization at announcement.
limitations: The capitalization is a dated Ripple statement, not a current independent measurement; RLUSD is a stablecoin and does not itself prove XRP demand.

observations.claim: Circle reported Q3 2026 Circle Mint customer flows of USD 104.304B minted and USD 103.694B redeemed, net +USD 610M; nine-month flows were USD 260.847B minted and USD 262.234B redeemed, net −USD 1.387B.
limitations: These are Circle Mint customer conversion flows, not total global USDC circulation changes, XRPL-only flows or XRP purchases.

observations.claim: Circle reported USDC market share of 27% versus 29% one year earlier and 7.35M meaningful wallets versus 6.34M; meaningful wallets are wallets holding more than USD 10 USDC and are not unique users.
limitations: Retain Circle's defined comparison universe; wallet counts do not equal people or active users.

observations.claim: As of 2026-09-30, approximately 84% of USDC reserves were held in the Circle Reserve Fund, a Rule 2a-7 government money-market fund managed by BlackRock, with Circle as its only shareholder; Circle states the fund is not FDIC/government insured or guaranteed and BlackRock has no obligation to reimburse losses.
limitations: Issuer disclosure does not establish a current reserve stress event or loss; the remaining reserve portion is held across multiple banks and U.S. Treasuries outside the fund.

observations.claim: Circle recorded USD 331.3M Q3 and USD 986.6M nine-month 2026 distribution costs in connection with Coinbase agreements; Q3 reserve income was USD 657.6M, down 7.5% year over year, with Circle attributing approximately USD 106.5M of decline to a 61-basis-point fall in average yields.
limitations: Distribution costs are contractual economics, not direct XRP flows; reserve income depends on circulation and interest rates.

observations.claim: Coinbase's Q3 2026 Form 10-Q says it renewed its arrangement with Circle on the same terms and that average USDC held in Coinbase products reached an all-time high.
limitations: Coinbase product balances and the Circle arrangement are USDC economics, not evidence of XRP collateral or XRP trading demand.

observations.claim: Circle's 2025 Form 10-K describes the historic 2018 Centre consortium as a 50/50 joint venture and the 2023 restructuring that gave Circle sole governance of the stablecoin network while Coinbase retained a minority equity interest and contractual revenue-sharing rights.
limitations: The later Coinbase Q3 2026 filing is the primary source for renewal on the same terms; no exact Coinbase ownership percentage is inferred.

observations.claim: Evernorth's Q3 2026 filing reports approximately USD 91,397 unrestricted cash as of 2026-09-30 (rounded elsewhere to USD 0.1 million), a USD 10.0 million net working-capital deficit and USD 185.6 million accumulated deficit. It identifies Ripple loans and XRP contributed to Pathfinder as liquidity sources. This balance is not equivalent to gross transaction proceeds disclosed separately at closing.
limitations: Issuer-reported balances; no bank confirmation or post-2026-09-30 cash reconciliation captured.
Preserve legal-entity scope across subsidiary and post-transaction disclosures.

observations.claim: The filing states that Pubco raised USD 214.1 million in cash and received 261,919,096 XRP under private-placement subscription agreements; it says the USD 214.1 million cash proceeds were subsequently used to purchase 84,365,876 XRP. It reports approximately 346,284,972 XRP held by Evernorth as of 2026-09-30. This is historical financing/deployment disclosure, not a timestamped record of current-period exchange purchases.
limitations: No trade-level execution receipts, counterparties, venues or wallet transfers captured.
The filing does not establish whether every purchase was publicly executed or privately negotiated.

observations.claim: A separate transaction-closing disclosure reports approximately USD 272.6 million aggregate gross cash proceeds before transaction expenses, comprising approximately USD 224.6 million of private-placement investments and USD 48.0 million released from the SPAC trust after redemptions; investors also contributed approximately 388,910,554 XRP in kind. These closing figures must not be added to the earlier USD 214.1 million / 261,919,096 XRP subscription disclosure without reconciling periods, entities and possible overlap.
limitations: Gross closing proceeds are not net proceeds, current unrestricted cash or proof of spot-market XRP purchases.
Different reporting periods and transaction contexts require a funds-flow bridge.

observations.claim: The filing says a USD 30.0 million 4% PIK convertible note had not been issued as of 2026-09-30 because closing had not occurred; it also says Evernorth had not borrowed under its USD 1.0 million Ripple revolving facility as of that date. Neither amount should be treated as cash received or cash on hand at that cutoff.
limitations: Post-closing note issuance and subsequent facility draws require later filings or transaction receipts.
A committed or undrawn facility is not cash on hand.

observations.claim: The filing identifies Coinbase as the principal market used for XRP fair-value measurement and BitGo Trust as the initial third-party custodian for Pubco's XRP after the transactions. These disclosures establish accounting-valuation and custody roles, not an exclusive trading, market-making or execution relationship.
limitations: No custody statement, wallet address, exchange trade record or service agreement captured.
Principal-market designation does not establish that all purchases or sales occurred on Coinbase.

observations.claim: The exact phrase 'actual capital' does not appear in the cited SEC filing. The filing instead distinguishes unrestricted cash, gross closing proceeds, cash private-placement proceeds, XRP contributed in kind, XRP bought with cash proceeds, debt not yet issued and an undrawn revolving facility.
limitations: This finding is limited to the cited filing and does not establish that the phrase is absent from all Evernorth or XRP-related communications.

competing_hypotheses.claim: SBI Remit's ODL use with XRP may create real corridor-level XRP settlement demand.
disconfirming_or_missing: No corridor-level ODL volumes, XRP inventory, net settlement flow or collateral balances captured.
SBI Ripple Asia itself explicitly says it does not handle XRP.
RLUSD distribution and the tokenized-deposit PoC do not prove XRP use.
competing_hypotheses.test: Acquire authorized corridor-level ODL volume, XRP wallet/inventory and settlement timing data; separate gross throughput, net XRP held, third-party liquidity and market purchases.

competing_hypotheses.claim: SBI's Ripple-related activity is multi-rail: RippleNet software, ODL with XRP through separate entities, RLUSD distribution and a tokenized-deposit XRPL PoC can coexist without all activity creating XRP demand.
disconfirming_or_missing: Ripple describes ODL with XRP at SBI Remit and partners, so some genuine XRP use exists.
competing_hypotheses.test: Map each legal entity, product, settlement asset, ledger, corridor, counterparty and volume separately; do not aggregate RippleNet, RLUSD, XRPL and ODL.

competing_hypotheses.claim: Coinbase-Circle USDC distribution growth and reserve economics may affect dollar liquidity and exchange collateral conditions but do not establish direct XRP demand.
disconfirming_or_missing: No XRPL-specific USDC supply, XRP collateral, exchange-wallet flow or matched XRP order-book response captured.
Circle Mint flows are not total global USDC circulation changes.
competing_hypotheses.test: Build chain-specific USDC supply/mint/burn/bridge flows and exchange collateral balances, then test lagged XRP depth/returns against BTC, rates, USD and broad crypto controls.

competing_hypotheses.claim: Concentration of 84% of USDC reserves in a BlackRock-managed government money-market fund is a material reserve-structure and operational-dependency variable.
disconfirming_or_missing: The fund holds short-dated Treasuries, overnight Treasury repos and cash.
No reserve impairment, redemption stress or operational interruption established.
competing_hypotheses.test: Track fund composition, NAV, redemption liquidity, custody/settlement dependencies, bank cash concentration and stress-period redemption behavior.

competing_hypotheses.claim: The SBIC East/Central/West acronym can be mistaken for SBI Holdings, creating false corporate relationship edges.
disconfirming_or_missing: Official profiles identify distinct regional legal companies, founding dates and service areas; no SBI Holdings affiliation is shown in the cited profiles.
competing_hypotheses.test: Reconcile Japanese corporate registry identifiers, shareholder registers and official group-company lists before adding any ownership edge.

competing_hypotheses.claim: Coinbase and Circle have material USDC distribution and revenue-sharing interdependence that is economically important even without an XRP-specific link.
disconfirming_or_missing: The filings do not establish direct Ripple/SBI ownership or an XRP settlement channel.
Distribution costs and USDC platform balances are not XRP spot demand.
competing_hypotheses.test: Reconcile contract terms, renewal dates, platform balances, distribution-cost sensitivity, reserve yields and counterparty concentration across future SEC filings.

competing_hypotheses.claim: Evernorth financing headlines and gross transaction proceeds are not equivalent to cash on hand or incremental XRP spot demand. The filing separates pre-closing private-placement cash and XRP contributions, historical XRP purchases, post-closing gross proceeds, in-kind XRP, unissued debt and an undrawn facility.
disconfirming_or_missing: The filing reports USD 214.1 million of cash subscription proceeds used to purchase 84,365,876 XRP.
Post-closing cash proceeds could fund additional XRP purchases, but later trade-level evidence is absent.
In-kind XRP contributions can enlarge treasury holdings without creating contemporaneous spot buying pressure.
competing_hypotheses.test: Reconcile dated financing receipts, share issuance, in-kind XRP transfers, exchange executions, custody wallet movements and post-closing treasury purchases. Separate gross proceeds, net proceeds, cash balance, XRP inventory and market purchases.

data_quality.no_averaging_policy: Do not aggregate spot depth across venues or quote currencies, do not treat Circle Mint flows as total USDC supply, and do not map global USDC or RLUSD activity directly to XRP demand.
data_quality.raw_source_policy: Public pages and SEC filing text were read as rendered web content. Original HTTP wire bytes, headers, independent timestamps and immutable SHA-256 receipts were not captured in Barrot. All observations remain research-only and model-ineligible.
data_quality.source_independence: The three SBIC profiles are primary but related sister companies; SBI Holdings and Ripple are interested JV parties; SBI PoC and RLUSD announcements are issuer statements; Circle and Coinbase are separate SEC registrants and counterparties; Circle's 10-K and 10-Q are the same issuer, not independent corroboration. The Evernorth SEC filing is primary issuer-authored disclosure; it is not independent corroboration of bank receipts, market executions or on-chain transfers.
scope_warnings: SBIC is not SBI Holdings based on the cited legal identities and regional profiles; complete beneficial-ownership search remains open.
SBI Group aggregate voting rights are not the same as direct SBI Holdings parent ownership.
SBI Ripple Asia's explicit no-XRP statement must not be generalized to SBI Remit or SBI VC Trade.
RLUSD is a stablecoin and the MoneyTap/XRPL activity is a PoC; neither establishes XRP purchases or net XRP demand.
Circle Mint customer flows are not global USDC supply flows, XRPL-specific supply or XRP collateral.
Meaningful-wallet counts are wallets, not unique people.
Circle's 84% reserve-fund figure is dated 2026-09-30, not an intraday reserve audit.

The Evernorth filing contains multiple legal-entity, pre-closing and post-closing contexts. Keep USD 214.1M / 261.9M XRP subscription amounts separate from USD 272.6M gross closing cash / 388.9M XRP in-kind contributions until a funds-flow reconciliation rules out overlap.
